A1.justification: Both PDFs are readable versions of the same MobileManiBench work. Inspection covered all pages, including v1's supplementary Sections A–C. The supplied v2 ends at the references and omits most supplementary material; this is an observable omission, not an extraction failure.

before.justification: v1 reports original simulation experiments, model comparisons and ablations in Section 5, plus a real-world laptop-opening experiment achieving 40% success over 10 trials in Appendix C.

after.justification: v2 retains original simulation results, including MobileManiRL and MobileManiVLA success rates in Table 3, ablations in Tables 4–5 and 7, and model comparisons in Table 6.

M1.justification: The retained descriptions specify the same keypoint-based RL pipeline, reward structure, PaliGemma-2/DiT architecture, inputs, training objective and inference strategy. The redrawn architecture diagram corresponds to v1 Figure 7. Omitted supplementary specifications do not establish an actual algorithm change.

E1.justification: Simulation coverage remains two robots, 630 objects across 20 categories, five skills and 100 realistic scenes. The limited real-world G1 laptop-opening evaluation documented in v1 Appendix C is absent from v2, although a general reference to real-world inference remains.

E2.justification: Table 6 retains OpenVLA, CogACT, π0 and π0.5 with the same model sizes. Omitted Appendix Table 13 breaks down these same comparisons by category. BEHAVIOR-1K is added to the benchmark overview, not evaluated as a competing method.

E3.justification: The retained simulation splits, training budgets, episode counts and fixed-base comparison are unchanged. The real-world evaluation protocol disappears with Appendix C.2: 10 trials with randomized initial poses and the robot base initially 1 m from the laptop. Missing implementation settings do not establish changes to retained experiments.

E4.justification: The main modality, state-input, generalization and base-mobility ablations remain. v2 omits the category-level ablation evidence in Tables 10–12 and the real-world deployment case study. This reduces analytical detail without changing the principal simulation ablation questions.

E5.justification: Neither version reports confidence intervals, standard deviations, significance tests or repeated-training seed information. The omitted real-world experiment's 10 trials specify evaluation sample size, not a separate uncertainty-estimation procedure.

E6.justification: Tables 3–7 retain their values, and v1 Figure 4 is retained as the identical success-rate chart in v2 Figure 5. However, v2 removes the distinct category-level results in Tables 10–13 and the 40% real-world success result. Lost findings include π0 outperforming MobileManiVLA on cabinet tasks, 23.7% versus 22.3%, despite the opposite aggregate ranking.

T1.justification: v1 Appendix A.3 formally defines the reward components, grasp indicator and reference actions in Equations 3–10. These definitions disappear from v2, which retains only the aggregate reward and diffusion objective in Equations 1–2. This substantially reduces mathematical specification without demonstrating a changed method.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the same simulation-first verification contribution, benchmark scale, automated trajectory-generation claims and support for studying VLA architectures and modalities. The main claims are not narrowed to reflect the omitted supplementary evidence.

C2.justification: The eight main experimental takeaways remain. Omitted Appendix C.1 removes specific deployment limitations: unavailable wrist depth, degraded head-camera depth, use of an RGB-only variant, and restriction to laptop opening because other tasks performed poorly. These qualifications are absent despite the retained real-world generalization statement.

D1.justification: v2 loses extensive reproducibility information from Appendices A–C, including simulator setup, asset and grasp-point construction, depth normalization, the approximately 90M-parameter DiT-Base and 10-step DDIM specification, baseline learning schedules, action-execution settings and real-world preprocessing. Main training budgets remain. The project-site address also changes, without local evidence establishing availability.

R1.justification: v2 adds BEHAVIOR-1K to Table 1, cites RoboCerebra and resolves the G1 robot source citation. Isaac Lab and X-VLA references present in v1 disappear. The broader positioning relative to manipulation benchmarks and VLA research remains substantially unchanged.

P1.justification: The structured supplement containing Implementation Details, Experiment Details and Real-world VLA Inferences is removed, while several main-text pointers to the Appendix remain. This substantially changes document structure and completeness. Sections 1–6 otherwise retain their order and nearly all prose, with limited wording, keyword and corresponding-author edits.

P2.justification: v2 replaces the two-column layout with a single-column format and redraws and moves v1's supplementary architecture Figure 7 into the main text as Figure 4. Table 1 drops the object-category column and adds BEHAVIOR-1K. Supplementary Tables 8–13 and most supplementary figures disappear; the main success-rate chart is retained and renumbered.

improvement.justification: The clearer architecture diagram and limited citation improvements do not offset removal of essential reward definitions, reproducibility details, category-level evidence and the real-world experiment. v2 retains references to absent appendices and a real-world generalization statement without the reported 40% result or deployment restrictions. These omissions substantially weaken the supplied paper's reproducibility and evidential support, despite unchanged main results.
